title: Office 365 MCP Values
description: Values for the Office 365 MCP Helm chart. Python FastMCP server for Microsoft 365. Exposure uses base chart Gateway API routes (no custom Ingress).

mcpConfig.description: Configuration for the Office 365 MCP Server, mapped to environment variables (PUBLIC_BASE_URL, ENTRA_TENANT_ID, ENTRA_CLIENT_ID, TOOLS_PRESET/TOOLS_ENABLED).

publicBaseUrl.description: The externally-reachable OAuth issuer URL clients are redirected to. Must be https. Example: https://office-365.mcp.unique.app

entra.description: Entra app registration users sign in through

tenantId.description: The single tenant whose issuer every access token is validated against. A multi-tenant authority is rejected at startup.

clientId.description: The client ID of the Entra app registration users sign in through.

clientSecret.description: The app registration's client secret, from the office-365-mcp-entra-application Terraform module's client_secrets[key].key_vault_secret_name output. Also the key material for the OAuth state rows, so rotating it costs every signed-in user one re-login. fromSecretProvider is auto-collected into the chart's SecretProviderClass — no separate secretProvider.vaults entry needed.

tools.description: The tool surface this deployment runs. Set exactly one of preset or enabled — the tools enabled decide which delegated Microsoft Graph permissions every user is asked to consent to at sign-in, so there is deliberately no default: 'every tool' has to be a choice rather than what a deployment gets by not making one.

preset.description: Which tools this deployment runs, as a named surface. 'teams' is every Teams tool; each other name is one use case, and README's preset table says what each costs a tenant in permissions and admin consents. Set this or enabled, never both. Narrowing a live deployment is free; widening it makes every signed-in user sign in again.

enabled.description: Which tools this deployment runs, as a comma-separated list of tool names, for a surface no preset covers. get_me is always on and need not be listed, so no deployment asks for less than User.Read. Set this or preset, never both. Must name at least one tool: an empty value is a selection that says nothing, which the server refuses to start on, and catching it here is the difference between a failed helm install and a crash-looping pod. GET /manifest and the startup log print the resolved tools, the exact delegated permissions and which of them need admin consent — that list is what an Entra administrator has to grant.

folder.description: Grafana folder name for the dashboard
